audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer and the content layer disagreed on all seven level-chart rows, and the packet chart itself was flagged as contradicting the data: Azir wins 42.5% over 727 games but was given six of seven stages.
audit.why: The lane genuinely splits. Vladimir has no gap closer, no CC, and Tides of Blood costs him his own health, so Azir wins levels 1-5 on soldier range alone. From Hemoplague at six onward Crimson Pact turns every AP item into health, Transfusion is free on a 4.6s rank-5 cooldown, and Azir cannot remove him — which is where 42.5% comes from.
audit.corrected: Chart resolved to Azir / Azir / Azir / Azir / Vladimir / Vladimir / Vladimir. full phases[0..3].side moved Skill->Azir and phases[4].side moved Skill->Vladimir; content win[5] and win[6] moved Azir->Vladimir. Every affected why on both layers rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and spikes[3] both claimed Azir extends his lead at first item and full build, which contradicts both the win rate and the corrected chart.
audit.why: Crimson Pact gives 1 AP per 30 bonus health and 1.6 health per AP, so Vladimir's first item and every item after it buy him both stats. Transfusion costs 0 mana and drops to 4.6s at rank 5. Hemoplague is a flat 120s at all three ranks and heals him for each champion hit.
audit.corrected: spikes[2] rewritten around his first item outscaling your Nashor's; spikes[3] rewritten around Crimson Pact health stacking and the flat 120s Hemoplague. content mid and late rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated a single real interaction. It said Vladimir 'lands Sanguine Pool' and 'out-ranges your plan', both of which are false — Sanguine Pool is a self-cast escape and his longest ability is 625.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 350 range, 28/25/22/19/16s, two seconds untargetable — it is the escape you bait, not a threat you dodge. Transfusion and Tides of Blood are both 600 range against a soldier that attacks from further out, and Tides of Blood is explicitly blocked by units in the way and paid for in his own health. Vladimir has no CC at all, so Azir's Shifting Sands exit is never contested. His entire sustain runs on Transfusion at 0 mana, which is what makes Grievous Wounds timing decide every extended trade.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, tradeGood, tradeBad, dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[0].d with the real numbers. Anti-heal requirement written into winCon, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, loading, content mid and content late.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit — defect catalogue item 3.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool at 28s rank 1 is the single largest punishable cooldown in this lane and it was described only as 'untargetable dodge'.
audit.corrected: Rewrote with Sanguine Pool 28/25/22/19/16s, Tides of Blood 13s at rank 1, and Hemoplague flat 120s at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appeared only as a trailing clause in report[8].t and nowhere in the fields a player actually reads in champ select.
audit.why: Transfusion heals on a 4.6s cooldown at rank 5 for zero mana and Hemoplague heals him per champion hit. Without Grievous Wounds soldier chip damage is undone faster than it lands.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in winCon, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, loading, content mid and content late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed on dosFull[1].d (the tradeGood string verbatim) and dontsFull[2].d (the tradeBad string verbatim); dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d explained something unrelated to their titles; dontsFull[1].d cited a 19-second Shifting Sands when rank 1 is 22s.
audit.why: Defect catalogue items 2 and 6. The tradeBad string also asserted 'the engage window every Vladimir player is waiting for' — Vladimir has no engage.
audit.corrected: All five bodies rewritten to match their own titles with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave was Azir boilerplate identical to every other matchup.
audit.why: Against a champion with no CC, no dash and a self-damaging E, the correct wave is a hard shove from level 1 — the opposite of the 'controlled slow push' the template recommended.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around shoving pre-6 and crashing before the Hemoplague timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.carry and breakdown.late were all name-swap templates, and winCon claimed Azir out-scales Vladimir.
audit.why: Template sweep, plus a factual inversion: at 42.5% it is Vladimir who out-scales.
audit.corrected: Each regrounded on the early-window-or-nothing shape of the matchup.

audit.why: The packet flagged 'Use Sanguine Pool' at wants.foe[2] as a probable wrong ability name. It is a false positive — the kit file gives W as Sanguine Pool and the page spelled it correctly.
audit.corrected: No name change made. wants.foe[2] was edited for a different reason: it claimed Sanguine Pool dodges Azir's R cast, which I could not verify.

notes: Chart resolved as one unit: full phases[0..3].side Skill->Azir, phases[4].side Skill->Vladimir, content win[5] and win[6] Azir->Vladimir, with every affected why on both layers rewritten in the same proposal. Note that full phases[5] and phases[6] already read 'Vladimir' while their whys described Azir winning the stage — that is the 189-row defect and both whys are rewritten here. Ratings left untouched throughout: phases[N].rating appears to encode stage difficulty (the two Vladimir rows carry 7/10 against a 7/10 diffRating while neutral rows carry 5/10) but I did not want to guess that polarity. packet.suspectNames flagged 'Use Sanguine Pool' as a wrong ability name — false positive, the kit confirms W is Sanguine Pool. Unverified and therefore not written: whether Sanguine Pool's untargetability blanks Emperor's Divide's knockback (the old wants.foe[2] asserted it and I removed the claim), whether Sand Soldiers count as the 'enemy units' that block Tides of Blood, and whether soldier AoE damage applies to an untargetable Vladimir.
